LESSON: ANGLES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry
Topic 4.1: Angles
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Angles, part of Geometry in Grade 7 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: What are angles? 2. Where do we use angles in real-life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. relate different types of angles on a straight line in real-life situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Angles in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. solve angles at a point in learning situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Angles in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate angles on a transversal in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Angles in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. solve angles in a parallelogram in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Angles in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. identify angle properties of polygons up to hexagons in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Angles in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. relate interior angles, exterior angles, and the number of sides of a polygon up to hexagons in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Angles in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. relate different types of angles on a straight line in real-life situations

   Angles helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. solve angles at a point in learning situations

   Angles helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. relate angles on a transversal in different situations

   Angles helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. solve angles in a parallelogram in different situations

   Angles helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. identify angle properties of polygons up to hexagons in different situations

   Angles helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. relate interior angles, exterior angles, and the number of sides of a polygon up to hexagons in different situations

   Angles helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

G. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss positions of objects in the immediate environment in relation to angles

2. draw straight lines with different angles, measure, and relate them.

3. draw different angles at a point, measure, relate, and work out angles at point

4. draw transversals, measure and relate angles in a transversal

5. draw parallelograms, measure and relate various angles in a parallelogram

6. use cut-outs or drawings of different polygons up to hexagon, measure the interior angles, and relate to 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss positions of objects in the immediate environment in relation to angles
2. draw straight lines with different angles, measure, and relate them.
3. draw different angles at a point, measure, relate, and work out angles at point
4. draw transversals, measure and relate angles in a transversal
5. draw parallelograms, measure and relate various angles in a parallelogram
6. use cut-outs or drawings of different polygons up to hexagon, measure the interior angles, and relate to 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Angles together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses the positions of objects in the immediate environment in relation

to angles.

● Critical thinking and Problem-solving: as the learner draws, measures, and relates angles.

Values

● Responsibility: as the learner explores positions of objects in the immediate environment in relation to angles.

● Unity: as the learner works with peers to use cut-outs or drawings of different polygons up to hexagons.
